text:
Erin: Heads up — after rolling the new 4-bit kernel gating heuristic to canary yesterday we saw a throughput dip and a mem spike on the NF4 fleet. Graph: https://grafana.redwood/ci/4bit-gating (image). :frowning_face:
Raj: saw the alert too. Is this the gating change that avoids prefetch on small batches?
Erin: yes, the heuristic delays prefetch for sub-64 token sequences to reduce wasted work. Canary enabled at 03:15 UTC. Throughput for -nf4-370 dropped ~18% on tail p95.
Maria: I profiled one affected host with pprof. CPU looks fine; the allocator/kv-owner thread shows lots of small allocations sticking around. Suspect cache key churn.
Sasha: interesting — could be alignment of kv keys after quantization changes. NF4 padding pattern changed so prefix hashes differ more often. That would blow up KV entries.
Erin: exact logs from the host: 
```
[2024-11-09T03:20:12Z] runtime: kvcache_insert key=tok-prefix-0x7f82 len=56
[2024-11-09T03:20:12Z] runtime: kvcache_insert key=tok-prefix-0x12b9 len=64
[2024-11-09T03:20:13Z] runtime: kvcache_insert key=tok-prefix-0xa7e len=8
... repeated different prefixes per request
```
Erin: you can see keys are not shared which implies the prefix normalization we expected isn't applied post-quantization.
Raj: that explains memory ripple — allocator can't reuse slabs, slab fragmentation grows, scheduler sees free memory drop and gates more aggressively => throughput oscillation.
Maria: ran a lightweight heap dump: slab live objects up 3x vs baseline. Also noticed tighter clustering of short-lived allocations at the same addresses, hinting at churn instead of leak.
Sasha: quick repro? can we replay canary traffic against a debug build with KV key canonicalization enabled?
Erin: I set up a canary test. Patch branch: `gating-fix/kv-canonicalize`. It forces `normalize_prefix()` before hash. Small diff: 
```diff
- hash = murmur(prefix)
+ norm = normalize_prefix(prefix) // collapse pad/entropy tokens
+ hash = murmur(norm)
```
Erin: on local repro this reduces new key rate by ~78% and brings p95 throughput back within 3% of baseline.
Raj: good. Any downside? Could normalize be expensive (allocations/copy)?
Erin: implemented as inplace collapse with stack buffer for <=96 bytes. No allocations measured in perf traces.
Sasha: we should also add a metric for key-cardinality in kvcache so this doesn't slip.
Maria: Agreed. Add `kvcache.key_cardinality` and an alert if > 2x baseline sustained for 5m.
Erin: ops-bot, can you roll the gating heuristic off on canary while we promote the patch?
ops-bot: Received. Rolling back feature flag `4bit_gating_prefetch` on canary group now. rollout_id=ffb-420.
deploy-bot: rollback completed at 03:25 UTC on 8 hosts.
Raj: plan: 1) revert flag on canary (done), 2) promote `gating-fix/kv-canonicalize` to staging and run replay for 2h, 3) add cardinality metric/alert, 4) if green, re-enable with smaller cohort.
Sasha: add an A/B that measures new-key-rate and p99 latency per model-version so we can catch model-specific entropy patterns.
Erin: documenting notes in the incident tracker and will open a postmortem draft. Also we need to audit other heuristics that depend on token alignment (packing, batching).
Maria: FYI I ran a short experiment with forcing zero-padding normalization at the tokenizer stage (server-side) — that also reduced key churn but had edge cases for streaming callers. Might be useful as fallback.
Raj: nice. Timebox the full validation to today and aim to promote tonight if canary looks stable. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
